# Prefill scratch precision boundaries and reuse (R348)

**Scope.** Read-only source review of the Strata worktree pinned by the task to WC 410904c. No build, execution, GPU/model run, measurement, cleanup, or source change was performed. Values below are allocation payload arithmetic, not observed VRAM or a 16K fit claim. Alloc::take adds its alignment/guard allowance per allocation; allocator/page effects and unrelated live owners also affect actual residency.

## Current inventory and boundaries

For this artifact, `N=2560`, `D=C=10240`, `HC=4`, `LR=320`, `K=10`, `ZV=6144`, `HV=48`. Set sizing in `prefill.cpp` allocates one maximum of GDN, QSA, and MoE scratch; it does not add those three sets. Below are payload bytes per token (B/token), followed by size at T=8192; binary MiB. The default fallback MoE scratch totals 234,240 B/token plus 4*E logits, so it is the shared-region winner at these shapes (before checking model/options and allocator overhead).

| Owner | Main payloads | B/token | At T=8192 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Top-level prefill planes | emb 10,240 F32; R 40,960 F32; xn 16 F32; xn16 20,480 U16; lo 1,280 F32; lo16 640 U16; gated 40,960 F32; inj 16 F32; mixed 10,240 F32; mixed_bf/mixed_h 5,120 each U16; bo 10,240 F32; steps 16 I32 | 144,032 | 1,125.25 MiB |
| GDN alternative region | qkv 40,960 F32; z 24,576 F32; ab 384 F32; gate/beta 192 each F32; hbuf 40,960 F32; y 24,576 F32; y_h 12,288 U16 | 144,128 | 1,126 MiB |
| QSA alternative region | Kc/Vc 2,048 each F32; Qf 12,288 F32; q/attn 24,576 each F32; idx_raw 512 F32; q_idx 2,048 F32; attn_h 12,288 U16; ids cap*4; plus fixed selector scores and attention scratch | 75,392 + 4*cap | 589 MiB + fixed |
| MoE fallback region | logits E*4; route w/ids/slot/src 4*K*4; Xs K*N*2; GU K*1280*4; Hh K*640*2; Dm K*N*4; sgate/sup each 640*4; sh_h 640*2; shared N*4; sg 4 | 234,240 + 4E | 1,831 MiB + logits |

GDN sums to 144,128 B/token. QSA selector scores are `sel_batch * max_blocks * 4`; at the cited maximum 262,144-cell geometry (`sel_batch=256`, `max_blocks=65,538`) that is 67,110,912 bytes (64 MiB). Decode attention scratch is `attn_batch * (ceil(cap/64)*n_head*(HD+2)+64) * 4`; with `attn_batch=32`, `cap=2051`, `n_head=48`, `HD=48`, this is about 9.68 MiB. QSA also includes its per-token planes/ids; report exact model's `cap`, state-cell count, and alignment before claiming a byte total.

The optional BF16x2 low-part planes add 64,000 B/token (xn16_lo, lo16_lo, mixed_bf_lo). They are enabled by the selected BF16x2 mode, not part of the base table. Compact MoE scratch reduces Xs/GU/Hh row extents from T*K to T only, under pure FP16 fallback, no MMQ/debug-NaN, and in-order queue; Dm remains T*K*N FP32, so the set still costs 147,244 B/token plus logits. MMQ adds its own Q8/H payloads and changes which scratch applies.

Outside those counted planes, `init` also owns expert dequant buffers (`dq_gu`, `dq_d`; source comment gives 157 MB for group 16), route/bounds/ring staging, optional MMQ group/ring storage, PLE `T*N` embedding, and stage/KV allocations. Lazy GEMM conversion caches and one-time autotune allocations are not in the carved `Alloc` total. These must be added from the actual mode/device before making any fit claim.

## Precision boundary

GEMM entry points in `gemm.hpp` produce FP32 outputs with FP32 accumulation, while several inputs are already compact. The existing `xn16`, `lo16`, `mixed_bf`, `mixed_h`, `y_h`, `attn_h`, and `sh_h` are U16 activation representations; changing them to a smaller format is not an additional savings opportunity. `Hh` is already FP16. FP32 is currently required for GDN recurrence/state and its published `y`, QSA projections/selector/attention and scratch, router logits/weights, FP32 MoE output rows `Dm`, residual/mixed/output planes, and reductions/normalization/softmax accumulation. Do not infer that a GEMM's FP32 output can be overwritten by its compact input: consumers and intervening FP32 work define its lifetime.

## Liveness-only reuse candidates (no arithmetic or cast change)

* **emb / bo / ple_emb three-way reuse:** prior R312 identified these as same-sized `T*N` FP32 planes. Embedding is consumed by the initial broadcast before the embedding plane can be reused; PLE embedding is uploaded/consumed before the later output projection writes `bo`. A carefully staged alias can save two planes, `2*T*N*4` = 160 MiB at T=8192 and 320 MiB at T=16384. This is a prior candidate, not a new discovery. Preserve same queue/order dependencies and update count/carve sizing together.
* **GDN qkv / y reuse:** prior R143 proposed reusing qkv's `T*C` storage for y (`T*ZV`) after the convolution has consumed qkv, on the ordered stream. It saves `T*ZV*4` = 192 MiB at 8192, 384 MiB at 16384 within the GDN subregion. Confirm every GDN branch and lifetime before implementation; it only lowers the shared allocation if GDN is the maximum set.
* **QSA Kc/Vc as later attention scratch:** prior R143 raised reusing their storage after KV append. Current sizing has Kc+Vc at 4096 floats/token and attention scratch is fixed by cap/geometry, so an exact non-overlapping extent/lifetime proof is required. The QSA region is also only relevant to net allocation when it wins the max. Treat as unproven for this source; no byte saving is booked.

These are scratch layout changes, not numeric changes. A max-of-sets region means a local reduction may produce zero VRAM reduction if another set still dominates. Keep these savings separate from reducing storage precision.

## Lower-storage precision candidate

The only large previously identified output-store candidate is `Dm`: FP32 route-row results of size `T*K*N*4` (800 MiB at 8192; 1,600 MiB at 16384). U16 storage would save `T*K*N*2` (400/800 MiB respectively) if every GPU/CPU producer and `moe_combine` reader used the same representation. Accumulation may remain FP32, but conversion at store changes rounded values before route-weighted combination. This is a precision change and must not be grouped with liveness reuse. Prior R335/R301 already discuss this candidate; no new FP16/BF16 activation is proposed here. Do not shrink persistent GDN states or softmax/RMS/router reductions as “scratch.”

## Required evidence before accepting any numeric change

For Dm storage precision, compare full logits against the FP32 baseline on identical prompt/session/token history, record max/mean absolute and relative logit error, top-token/rank changes, and per-token NLL/cross-entropy deltas on fixed held-out text. Run two-generation tests (first and second continuation from preserved state), with exact build/device/model/settings and all prompt offsets recorded. Define acceptance thresholds before looking at the results; there is no universal threshold supplied by this source review. For context-length claims, run separate repeated held-out quality cases that actually consume positions across the entire 262,144-token context, including the final positions, and report task-level outcomes and NLL there; a successful allocation or a short-window logit comparison does not establish long-context quality. Keep results distinct from pure alias validation. No quality or fit result is claimed in this report.

## Prior-art delta

R335/R301 cover Dm reduced storage; R312 covers the emb/bo/PLE three-plane alias; R143 covers the GDN qkv/y and proposed QSA reuse; R204 covers already-compact intermediate precision; R331 establishes full-logit comparator evidence. This report consolidates their boundaries against the current source inventory, corrects the QSA attention scratch arithmetic from the source formula, identifies Dm as still FP32 under compact MoE mode, and records that alias savings are clipped by the shared max-set allocator. It does not claim novel candidates or measured capacity.
